findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how seeded cached PASS credits survive the PRIMARY-SUCCESS branch (completion_recovery.py:506-514, which currently calls bank.discard() unread), not only the exhaustion/finalizer path — e.g. merge the seeded bank into the primary's structured output before discard, or route a credited run through the full-coverage merge regardless of primary success/exhaustion.
evidence: Plan: 'still-valid entries are SEEDED into the run's CriterionBank verbatim, so the bounded search targets only unproven criteria'; plan's finalizer-interaction reasoning and RED test cover only merge_finalizer_with_bank, which runs on the recovery/exhaustion path
completion_recovery.py:506-507: 'Primary SUCCESS: the structured output is authoritative; the bank is discarded unread. bank.discard()' — seeded credits in the bank are never read on the success path
completion_recovery.py:730 _finalize reads bank.all() only on the exhaustion/recovery branch, not on primary success
findings.finding: The credit-vs-evaluate protocol seeds cached PASS records into the run-scoped CriterionBank and drives reuse through the finalizer merge, but does not address the PRIMARY-SUCCESS branch where the bank is discarded unread and only the primary's own structured output is authoritative — so a primary that skips seeded criteria and then succeeds would drop the seeded credits (partial coverage) rather than credit them.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (Credit-vs-evaluate protocol) vs completion_recovery.py:506-514 (primary-success branch) and :730 (finalize uses bank.all())
scenarios: A re-verify where the seeded credits reduce the unproven set enough that the primary now COMPLETES within budget (the intended win): the primary emits a verdict covering only the unproven criteria; bank.discard() drops the seeded PASSes; the merged verdict is partial-coverage or the seeded criteria revert to unverified

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the cross-run cache entry schema (version field) and the seed-time fallback for a corrupt/unreadable/schema-mismatched cache file: fail-OPEN (ignore the entry, re-verify that criterion) rather than fail-loud, and state which schema_version the cache keys on.
evidence: Plan: cache entries 'store the FULL banked record (met, evidence text, citations)' and are 'SEEDED into the run's CriterionBank verbatim'
completion_banking.py:514-518 — bank._read raises CompletionRecoveryError('unrecognized banked-verdict schema') when schema_version != BANK_SCHEMA_VERSION
The plan gives an atomic-write and last-write-wins contract for the WRITE path but no read-side schema/version or corrupt-entry fallback for the SEED path
findings.finding: The new cross-run verdict cache stores 'the FULL banked record (met, evidence text, citations)' but the plan never specifies a schema_version for cache entries nor the fallback when a cache file is corrupt, unreadable, or carries a stale/unrecognized schema at seed time. The existing run-scoped bank's _read fails LOUD (raises CompletionRecoveryError, aborting recovery) on an unrecognized schema_version; a cache that PERSISTS across rebar versions will predictably meet stale-schema entries, and inheriting fail-loud would abort the whole re-verify — the opposite of the 'exhaustion converges across runs' intent.
findings.location: Plan step 3 (cross-run PASS-verdict cache); AC line 3 (re-verify credits cached PASS)
scenarios: A rebar upgrade changes BANK_SCHEMA_VERSION; a re-verify seeds an old cache entry and either aborts (fail-loud inherited) or silently mis-seeds
A partially-written or manually-corrupted cache JSON is encountered at seed time
findings.suggested_fix: State that each cache entry carries its own schema_version; at seed (completion_recovery.py CriterionBank.for_run path) a missing/mismatched/corrupt entry is skipped fail-open (that criterion re-verifies) and never aborts the run, distinct from the run-scoped bank's fail-loud _read.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define a RETIRE/cleanup path for completion_verdicts cache entries (e.g. prune entries whose fingerprint no longer matches on write, or a per-ticket max-entries/TTL sweep) so stale files do not accumulate.
evidence: '.rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/<criterion-hash>.json, written ONLY on a validated PASS record at finalize'
No sentence describes eviction, TTL, max-entries, or removal of entries whose fingerprint has rotated
Invalidation is described as a key-miss (new fingerprint -> new key), which leaves the old file on disk
findings.finding: The new ticket-scoped verdict cache defines CREATE (write on validated PASS), CONSUME (seed at run start), and staleness invalidation (fingerprint key change), but no RETIRE/cleanup path — superseded entries (old fingerprints for a criterion whose material changed) become key-misses yet are never pruned from .rebar/cache/completion_verdicts/<ticket>/, so the cache accumulates dead JSON files indefinitely.
scenarios: A ticket re-verified many times across evolving code accretes one stale verdict file per fingerprint rotation, unbounded
